items.title: Build your immunity to fight COVID: Lemon juice in warm water
items.snippet_en: An article from IndiaToday.in states that lemon juice in warm water can boost immunity and fight cold/flu due to Vitamin C and antioxidants, but does not claim it destroys coronavirus.

items.title: Report coronavirus 'quack cures' immediately, says UK government
items.snippet_en: The Guardian reported on March 26, 2020, that the UK government urged people to report "dangerous quack cures" for coronavirus, including lemon juice, liquid silver, and hot water.

items.title: Common Myths About Coronavirus Explained
items.snippet_en: Hackensack Meridian Health stated on March 3, 2020, that there is no evidence that home remedies like lemon juice are effective against COVID-19 or any other virus.
The Associated Press debunked the claim on April 2, 2020, stating that drinking hot water with lemon is not a cure for coronavirus.

items.title: COVID-19: Popular Food Myths Busted - Lemon Water
items.snippet_en: NDTV reported on May 5, 2021, that the claim of hot water and lemon killing coronavirus was fact-checked by PIB and found to be false.
A Facebook post from May 3, 2020, clarified that drinking lemon juice or water will not kill COVID-19, and the theory about acidic environments is incorrect.

items.title: Lemon Juice Does Not Cure COVID-19
items.snippet_en: The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine published on April 22, 2020, that consuming acidic drinks like lemon juice has no effect on coronavirus infections.

items.title: Coronavirus Pandemic: Acid Kill COVID-19 Takeout Food? Dr. Mallika Marshall WBZ-TV
items.snippet_en: CBS News on May 5, 2020, confirmed that consuming acidic liquids will not kill the coronavirus.
St. Vincent's Hospital stated on June 24, 2020, that you cannot change the pH inside your body to fight off coronavirus by sucking a lemon or drinking lemon-infused water.

items.title: The Infodemic: Lemon Juice Won't Cure COVID-19
items.snippet_en: VOA News published an article on May 18, 2021, titled "The Infodemic: Lemon Juice Won't Cure COVID-19."
A YouTube video from April 27, 2020, featuring a microbiology expert, explained that lemon water cannot penetrate and kill the virus inside cells.

items.title: False claims drinking water, lemon can prevent COVID-19 circulate online
items.snippet_en: AFP reported on March 12, 2020, that consuming a high amount of vitamin C has never been proven effective against coronavirus.

outputs.notes_en: Multiple sources contradict the claim that drinking hot water with lemon juice will destroy the coronavirus. While lemon water may offer some health benefits, it is not effective against COVID-19.
